```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("rvis-setup.R")
```

In a shiny app or an rvis dashboard, a click on an item of a chart (a node or link of a graph, a
bar, a point, a slice, a table cell or a map marker) can set a shiny input, so that other outputs
react to it: show the details of the clicked node, filter a table by the clicked bar, zoom a map.

`rvisClickEvents()` adds this to a chart. It adds a small javascript function to the htmlwidget with
`htmlwidgets::onRender()`, which runs after the plotting package has drawn the chart: the javascript
of the plotting package is not copied or changed, so new versions of the package keep working.

## In a shiny app

Wrap the chart in `rvisClickEvents()`. A click then sets `input$<output id>_item_click`:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(rvis)

ui <- fluidPage(
  echarts4r::echarts4rOutput("bars"),
  verbatimTextOutput("clicked"))

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$bars <- echarts4r::renderEcharts4r({
    deaths <- data.frame(age = rownames(VADeaths), VADeaths, check.names = FALSE)
    rvisClickEvents(rvisPlot("bar", "echarts", obj = deaths, x = "age", y = list("Rural Male", "Urban Male")))
  })
  output$clicked <- renderPrint(str(input$bars_item_click))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

A click on the *70-74* bar of the *Rural Male* series gives:

```
List of 9
 $ type  : chr "point"
 $ id    : chr "70-74"
 $ label : chr "70-74"
 $ series: chr "Rural Male"
 $ index : int 4
 $ value : num 66
 $ x     : chr "70-74"
 $ y     : num 66
 $ widget: chr "bars"
```

The input is set again on every click, also when the same item is clicked twice. Give another input
name with argument `inputId`.

## In a dashboard

Give an output item the field `click.events: true`: the chart returned by its service sends its clicks
to input `<item name>_item_click`, used by the services of other items like any input. The example
dashboard [`click-events`](dashboard-reference.html#clicks) shows a graph and a bar chart and the items
clicked on them:

```{r, echo=FALSE}
x <- readLines(rvisDashboardExample("click-events"), warn = FALSE)
knitr::asis_output(paste0("```yaml\n", paste(x, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n"))
```

Run it with `runDashboard(rvisDashboardExample("click-events"))`.

## What a click gives

The value of the input is a list. Field `type` says what was clicked, and the other fields are given
as available:

| Field | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| `type` | `"node"`, `"link"`, `"point"` (bars, points, slices), `"cell"` (tables), `"marker"` or `"shape"` (maps), `"element"` (selector mode) |
| `id` | id of the item: node key, category, row name, marker `layerId`, ... |
| `label` | text shown for the item |
| `series` | series (or group) of the item |
| `index` | position of the item in its series |
| `value`, `x`, `y` | value and coordinates of the item |
| `source`, `target` | ends of a link |
| `row`, `column` | row number (as in R) and column name of a table cell |
| `lat`, `lng` | clicked point of a map |
| `group`, `depth`, `parent` | group of a node or marker, level and parent in a hierarchy |
| `data` | the d3 data of the clicked element (networkD3 and selector mode) |
| `widget` | id of the chart |

## Supported charts

| Plotter (package) | Clickable items | Notes |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `grviz` (DiagrammeR) and `DiagrammeR::grViz()` | nodes, edges | nodes of rvis grviz graphs are reported by their key |
| `networkD3` | nodes, links | sankey, force and tree networks |
| `echarts` (echarts4r) | all chart items | all chart types, including graphs and sankeys |
| `apexcharter` | bars, points, slices | |
| `plotly` | points, bars | |
| `highcharter` | points, bars, slices | |
| `amCharts` (rAmCharts) | bars, points, slices | rAmCharts charts are converted to htmlwidgets by `rvisClickEvents()`; `rAmCharts::renderAmCharts()` needs `library(rAmCharts)` |
| `c3`, `billboarder` | bars, points, slices | found under the transparent event layer of these charts |
| `visNetwork` | nodes, edges | |
| `DT` | table cells | `row`, `column`, `value`, and the row name as `id` |
| `dygraphs` | points | the series nearest to the pointer; the date as the chart shows it |
| `leaflet` | markers, shapes | including layers added later, for example by `leafletProxy()` |
| `coffeewheel` (rvis) | sunburst arcs | `name`, `value`, `depth`, `parent` |

Some packages also set inputs of their own (like `input$<id>_click` of DiagrammeR and billboarder, the
`event_data()` of plotly or the `_marker_click` inputs of leaflet). They keep working: rvis uses its own
input name, `<id>_item_click`, which has the same form for all charts.

## Any other widget: a CSS selector

For any other htmlwidget, give the CSS selector of its clickable elements:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
output$sun <- sunburstR::renderSunburst(
  rvisClickEvents(sunburstR::sunburst(sequences), selector = "path"))
```

The input then gets the id of the clicked element (its `data-id` attribute, svg title or id), its text,
and its d3 data in field `data`. Elements under a transparent layer, or which ignore the pointer, are
found too.

## Good to know

- Charts whose packages bring different versions of the d3 javascript library cannot share a page:
  for example coffeewheel (d3 version 3) with networkD3, or c3 with billboarder. This is a limit of the
  packages, not of the click events.
- dygraphs selects a point when the pointer moves over the plot: a click without moving the pointer
  first gives no point.
- A failure of the click javascript is written as a warning in the browser console and never stops the
  chart, or the other charts of the page, from being shown.
